<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The root cause is likely that `liveSession` is stored in in-memory module state. This would prevent the mobile browser session from reaching OBS.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Documentation appears to contain a critical clue.

OBS viewer tokens require an allowed origin matching the OBS page itself. A mobile publisher likely uses a different origin, so the viewer cannot subscribe to its stream.

The static client token is valid for five minutes, so a brief delay between minting and subscribing should not cause expiry. The origin mismatch remains the more likely culprit.

The code fetches the subscribe token immediately after connecting. This timing should satisfy the documentation requirement that the token be available before subscribing.

Five successful 204 responses confirm the subscribe token existed before the connection. The room then disconnected with CLIENT_INITIATED, suggesting the studio page reloaded and triggered a full teardown. The wasConnected flag being false may indicate the signaling socket closed during cleanup, or a second connection attempt occurred.

The server logs show only status polls. The current phone session is not publishing to this server. The phone may be connected to a different server instance. Alternatively the session may have disconnected before the log tail began.

No 403 errors appear in the logs, ruling out an origin mismatch blocking the phone. The missing session POSTs may simply be buried under the constant status poll traffic. I will search the full log file to verify whether the phone ever actually reached this server.

Only one Next.js server instance is running on port 3000. The phone may have used a local IP address such as 192.168.x.x, which is likely absent from APP_ORIGINS and would trigger a 403. If it had used the ngrok URL instead, the requests would have appeared in the logs.

A stale Next.js cache on the phone could be serving an old session. Mobile may report "connected" without actually publishing. React Strict Mode is also suspected: it triggers an immediate cleanup on mount that sets the generation counter and disconnects the session.

Desktop hot-reload may be killing the mobile session. Logs show ChunkLoadError and full page reloads. The user might see a frozen last frame or their local camera and think the call is active. This would explain why the mobile call does not appear on OBS.

I will run a targeted test to confirm whether module duplication is splitting the stores. I will POST a session from localhost with a fake subscribe token and check the status endpoint. If live is still false after a successful 204, the stores are duplicated. I also need to verify valid model names and session ID formats.
</details></think>

The network filter showed no API requests. Only a static note appeared.

The HMR error "Router action dispatched before initialization" caused full page reloads. This broke the mobile browser session. The console shows stale errors from the old session. The page is now on the OBS URL.

The phone's ngrok connection has a flaky HMR socket. File edits trigger HMR refreshes before the router initializes. Next.js throws and reloads the page. This unmounts the studio and disconnects the Decart call. The experimental mcpServer flag did not prevent this crash.

The user should hard-refresh the phone studio, start the call, and leave it open. They must not save files while the call is live. The OBS browser source also needs refreshing. The code fixes only help once the page stays open. I will check whether the OBS page polls for updates.

The HMR websocket error suggests the new server may be unhealthy. I will check the server terminal for status logs. Viewer JavaScript loading would still generate those logs even if HMR is broken.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The root cause is a blocked cross-origin request to the Next.js development HMR endpoint. This blocks the video stream from reaching OBS.

Next.js blocks requests from `127.0.0.1` because the dev server was started with `--hostname 0.0.0.0`. The browser source in OBS likely uses `127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost`, which explains why the stream never reaches OBS.
